claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

  - Child is fostered but the council is not paying for accommodation or maintenance
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment by getting the first question for you.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To help you, I need to understand your situation. Let me ask you about the child or children you're claiming for.

**First, how old is the child you're claiming Child Benefit for?**

Please tell me:
- The child's name (or names if you have more than one child)
- Their age(s)

The age is important because it affects eligibility:
- **Under 16**: Generally qualifies
- **16-19 years old**: May qualify if they're in approved education or training
- **20 or over**: Not eligible

Please share these details with me.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm inquiring about my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great to hear about Alex. Since he's 8 years old, he falls into the under 16 category, which is positive for Child Benefit eligibility.

Let me continue through the assessment by checking the next requirement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to ask: **Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

Since Alex is 8 years old, I expect he's not working. Just confirming this for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all. He's only 8, so he's just at primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's what I expected. Since Alex is 8 and not working, let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check: **Is Alex NOT receiving any benefits in his own right?** 

For clarity, this means benefits like:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit (in his own name)

At 8 years old, this would be unusual, but I need to confirm for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a child.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to ask: **Is Alex in any kind of apprenticeship?**

At 8 years old, this is very unlikely, but I need to confirm for completeness.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship. He's only 8 years old, so he's just in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's what I expected. Let me move forward with the next stage of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check your residency situation. This is an important requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Can you tell me about where you live and your residency status?**

Specifically:
- Do you normally live in the UK?
- If not in the UK, do you have any special status (such as EU Settlement Scheme status, or are you a Crown servant)?

Any of these situations could qualify you:
- Normally living in the UK
- Settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- Pre-settled status with specific circumstances (working, studying, seeking work, etc.)
- Crown servants living abroad in certain countries

What's your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK. I live here in England with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's straightforward - you meet the residency requirement. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to confirm: **Are you responsible for Alex's upkeep?**

This means you either:
- Live with him (which you've already told me you do), OR
- Contribute to his care and upkeep (food, clothes, housing, pocket money, etc.)

Since you mentioned Alex lives with you at home, I can confirm you're responsible for him. Let me proceed.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to ask: **Is there anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or anyone else who might claim?**

Specifically:
- Is another parent or guardian also claiming Child Benefit for him?
- If there is another person, have you both agreed who should be the main claimant?

Please let me know your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me looking after him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check Alex's living situation. **Is Alex:**

- Living normally at home with you?
- In hospital?
- In care?
- Being fostered?

Please let me know his current living arrangement.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, I'm fostering Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying that - that's important information. Let me continue with the assessment for fostered children.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
This is an important question for fostered children: **Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words:
- Is the council providing payments to cover Alex's accommodation and/or maintenance costs?
- Or are you covering these costs yourself without council payments?

Please let me know.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything. I don't get anything from the council to foster him - I'm covering all his costs myself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's good to know. Let me proceed to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Just to confirm one more time for this final check: **The local council is NOT paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance costs - you're covering everything yourself, correct?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's correct - the council isn't paying for his accommodation or maintenance. I'm covering everything myself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Wonderful! Based on all the information you've provided, I can now give you your eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Now let me provide you with your final eligibility outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 **You Are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex!**

### Summary of Your Situation:
You have successfully met all the eligibility requirements for claiming Child Benefit for Alex:

✅ **Alex's age**: 8 years old (under 16)
✅ **Not working**: No paid work exceeding limits
✅ **Not receiving benefits**: No benefits in his own name
✅ **Not in disqualifying apprenticeship**: Living normally
✅ **Your residency**: Normally living in the UK
✅ **Your responsibility**: You are responsible for Alex and he lives with you
✅ **No other claimants**: You're the only person claiming
✅ **Fostering arrangement**: Council is not paying for his accommodation or maintenance

### Next Steps - How to Claim:

1. **Apply online** at www.gov.uk/child-benefit or **by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide required documents**:
   - Proof of your identity
   - Alex's birth certificate
   - Your national insurance number
3. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge**: If you or a partner earns over £60,000 per year, there may be tax implications
4. **Payment frequency**: You'll receive payments every 4 weeks

### Additional Information:
For more details, visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Congratulations! You're eligible to claim, and Alex's fostering arrangement with full financial support from you qualifies perfectly for Child Benefit. Good luck with your application!

All eligibility criteria have been met.
arguments.overall_reasoning: You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex. As his foster carer, you meet all the necessary requirements: Alex is under 16, lives with you in the UK, you are responsible for his full upkeep with no council payments, and no other person is claiming for him. You can proceed to apply for Child Benefit."
